current_answer: As of 28 October 2026, public evidence does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models. BridgeBench’s latest visible NerfBench session is dated 16 October: GPT-6 Astra scored 97.1%, GPT-6.1 Sol 98.0%, Claude Sonnet 5.5 98.9%, and Claude Opus 5.5 105.8% of their first tracked sessions, all inside the publisher’s 90–110% band. Opus 5.5 rose 10.1 points from 95.7% on 9 October, but the score combines correctness, output tokens, and cost, and the board does not show which component moved. OpenAI’s 26 October notes add GPT-6.1 Terra to Work/Codex; some eligible users may see a changed default effort/model preset. Anthropic’s Gmail connector errors were resolved at 05:48 UTC on 28 October, with the provider reporting impact through 05:29 UTC. These product and service changes do not establish a decline in completed answers. Record the exact surface, selected model, effort, context, quota state, and task result before switching.

catalogue_card.text: No confirmed drop. NerfBench’s latest displayed Opus 5.5 score rebounded to 105.8% on 16 October, inside its 90–110% band. The score combines correctness, tokens, and cost; the page shows no newer session by 28 October.

summary: Broad capability decline across popular models is not established as of 28 October 2026.
BridgeBench’s latest visible NerfBench session is dated 16 October; all four displayed series are within the publisher’s 90–110% band.
Claude Opus 5.5 moved from 95.7% on 9 October to 105.8% on 16 October; the composite combines correctness, output tokens, and cost.
The board does not display component scores or task outputs, and the visible histories do not show its stated three sessions per week.
OpenAI’s 26 October release notes describe GPT-6.1 Terra rolling out in Work/Codex and a default Power preset change for some eligible Plus/Pro users.
Anthropic’s Gmail connector error window ended by 05:29 UTC on 28 October and was marked resolved at 05:48; this is a service-path event, not an answer-quality measure.
For a user decision, record surface, model, effort, context, task completion, and any limit/fallback; compare correctness and correction cost separately.
uncertainty: NerfBench’s 50 tasks and session outputs are private; the public board exposes only composite percentages, and the first tracked session is not shown to coincide with a model launch.

The 90–110% band and two-session rule are publisher methodology. The stated sampling illustration addresses a 70%-pass model, but the method does not publish calibration across other baseline rates or dependence across repeated fixed tasks.

The latest NerfBench session shown is 16 October; its public chart does not show the stated three tests per week. Whether sessions are missing from publication or testing cadence differed is unresolved.
OpenAI’s release notes and Anthropic’s incident history establish what the providers published, not a particular account’s route or outcome.
The new Gemini post and limit tracker are self-selected audience signals without representative denominators, matched tasks, or evidence of willingness to pay.
First-party pool analytics were unavailable, so page use, return visits, switching, sharing, follows, and funding remain unknown.
